Okay so, me and friends played this last night for about 3 hours or so, and I have a lot to say about this game already, and most of it is positive.

First: This game is really fun with friends. Even if it's just one or two other friends, it's fun. I love the text to speech, I've always proximity chat in games, has always made them more fun, like Lethal Company and Content Warning. 

Second: I like this game a little bit more than the other leading competitors in this genre of games, aka, Lethal Company, Content Warning, etc. I am not putting down those two games at all either by the way, me and my friends have enjoyed those games equally as much as we enjoyed this game too. But, there's something so specific about this game that makes it a real blast of a time. I personally love the fact that there really isn't a time limit when you're in the mission, you can explore and take as much time as you need. I love that you can revive your teammates in a few different ways that I have found, (putting their heads in the cash out spot, and when you bring it back to the truck). Makes the game feel like you don't really have to worry too much about dying. I also love the end area, where if you don't complete a mission and fail, you get sent into a "Last One Standing" fight arena, where you box up your friends and crown the winner.

This game so far, even after only one day or release, has a lot of soul, heart, and love put into it, and I really hope that the Dev team either sees this review, or even just sees the Overwhelmingly Positive reviews on the Steam Page, and continues their best and hardest to make this game even more fun, and me and my friends will continue to come back to it every single time.

Whenever I see that a game is as hyped up as R.E.P.O, I approach it with so much caution. High expectations can easily lead you to be disappointed, even if the game is actually good. I avoided it for a while but when my friend and I were in desperate need of a new game, I finally took the plunge for R.E.P.O and god damn I wish I had got this sooner. There is no disappointment at all because this more than lives up to the hype!!!

Pro's:

+ You can actually get revived mid round, so it's not a guarantee death will have you watching on and sadly munching on popcorn, as you wait to see if your team lives or dies.
+ We haven't exactly gotten too far since we play as a team of two and we're still learning, but it seems relatively well balanced with achievable quota's. We've had problems with other games where we know for sure it'll be game over when we hit a certain point
+ Really cool monster design. We haven't seen them all yet but there's so much 'What the hell is that???' yelling when we play. They seem to have pretty unique mechanics to them. 
+ Having an upgrade system to boost your stats is a great idea for a game like this
+ Nice QOL thing where once you hit the quota, you can check your map to help find your way out. The map is also super useful in general.
+ Super fun little mini game after a team K.O that will definitely bring out the worst in you
+ The game is hilarious to play. My jaw was actually aching after a three hour session because I'd been laughing my ass off for so long. Those big eyes and crouches just broke me each time and the fact you can pick a crouching party member up? Love it! Put my friend on the top shelf in the shop and threw him to his death at one point.
+ Unique items. I love how picking up certain things can trigger certain things to happen.
+ Teamwork can actually be optimal! Usually it's a split up to cover more ground type of things but when you're needing to drag a huge ass item around, you got to work together... and yell a little when one of you accidentally smashes it against a wall because they moved too carelessly. 
+ I love the designs of the places you explore! All unique from each other and different in theme
+ Actually a little scary sometimes. I have run screaming from a room once or twice... or five times... or ten...
+ The duck!!!! Love that lil fella, even if he killed my friend one time...and maybe me

Neg:

- ??? I know no game is perfect and that it will have them but I honestly can't think of any right now.

This game is just so much fun to play and it has a cute charm to it too. It's a game you can tell so much love and time was put into it, and it's such a blast to play. I'm so glad that it was able to gain such attention because it honestly deserves it.

Funny and entertaining? Yes! Accessibility? We need to talk about it...

Hello Steam community and potential developers of the game who may be reading this comment. To shorten the point for some here, I'll be brief: the game is extremely fun, the multiplayer mode is incredible and has already given me almost 30 hours of pure enjoyment! I recommend it 100%

Now, let's talk about another subject, accessibility. In my games, I wanted to get a friend of mine who is deaf to join in, as we saw that it was “possible” to play together in certain ways (speaking through the keyboard, agreeing that movement means danger and so on). But it still seems that the game isn't 100% able to attract/reach this community. Honestly, something like text accessibility notifying you that something has exploded, monster footsteps, Duck's quack and so on would be a huge improvement!

My deaf friend also gave me some tips such as:

- Putting indication signs when an enemy is near you, or an exclamation mark on an ally's head to warn of danger;
- It would also be nice to have an easy-to-read chat with written texts, because I thought the subtitles were too fast - each word disappeared too quickly.

So I beg you, bring some updates on accessibility for the deaf community! Few games take such care, so I'd love to see R.E.P.O as a game where everyone can have fun together :)

Bought R.E.P.O. thinking it was a co-op horror game.
What I got instead was:
a piano that weighs approximately the same as the moon
a friend who dropped a priceless ceramic vase down the stairs immediately
a monster that only activates when someone says "is it safe"
and a cart we lost in the first two minutes and never spoke of again.
The objective is simple. Carry valuable items carefully to extraction. Do not break them. We have never once done this.
The physics system is a masterpiece of human suffering:
"Okay, careful, careful—"
The vase flies sideways into a wall.
It was worth $4,000.
We needed $4,000.
Dave is no longer allowed to touch things.
The proximity voice chat adds incredible immersion. You can hear your friends whispering in real time as you creep through a dark mansion. You can also hear the exact moment someone starts screaming because a monster that looks like a rejected Pixar villain walked through a door at 2% speed and somehow this is the most terrifying experience of our collective lives.
The monster AI is elegantly simple. It hears noise. We make noise. This is our entire relationship with death.
The upgrade shop offers meaningful progression. We bought better lungs. We needed better lungs because we keep screaming. We are still screaming. We just have more health while we do it.
10/10.
We never hit quota.
We're going back in.

I play solo because all my gamer friends disappeared or never existed so I jumped into Repo through quick play fully expecting chaos and yep, chaos happened  but the fun kind!

Even without a squad, the game is super enjoyable. You can sneak, run, mess up horribly, and somehow still feel like a legend. The missions keep things moving, the tension builds in a fun way, and even when things go wrong (and they will), it’s hilarious, not frustrating.

Random teammates were mostly chill, and honestly? Half the fun is seeing how well you can all coordinate without saying a single word. Spoiler: not well, but it's still a good time.

If you’re a solo player wondering if you’ll have fun — yes. Panic, steal stuff, run like heck. 10/10 would scream silently again.

If you take a look at the steampage of R.E.P.O with it's silly banner and you think to yourself "Oh, another horror-coop loot-collection game? Why should I spent money, when I already have a few games like that?" I'll try to help your inner spending-demon find arguments to purchase this game regardless.

R.E.P.O is a horror-coop game that gives the loot-collection genre a new and exciting twist by being a 100 percent physics based game. What that means is, that the objects you interact with (and also you and your friends little roboter characters) will react to their environment. 
The objects you collect to pay the mysterious AI "Taxman" can and WILL break. You will definitely scream at your friends for breaking a 1.200$ vase. You can also get your revenge, by pushing the loot cart (yes, you don't need to carry ALL the loot by yourself) into your friends and make them ragdoll through the level. 
It also has fantastic mechanics like voice changing effects, funny easter eggs and a VERY funny text-to-speech option. There is nothing funnier than hearing your friend, crouched from under a table and hiding from a cute monsterous duck, say "Only an idiot says quack" over this feature. 

Other than that I recommend you check out the games studio on YouTube, where they are very open in the communication regarding the games plans and issues. (Latest one being about match-making lobbies, that are currently in active developement) Semiwork seems to be an aspiring studio that loves the games they make and try to stick with them and polish them, until they are done. (Planned features being character customazation, more level design and new enemies, ...)

I remember there was a developer commentary in Portal 2 that said one of the things players in co-op enjoyed the most was passing companion cubes to each other. Now imagine a whole game built around that mechanic. Not only can you throw items, use them as weapons, or carry big objects together (and then break them right before the extraction point), you can do that with yourself, your teammates, or even enemies. There are few interactions in gaming funnier than trying to grab an enraged enemy together and smack it against the wall. Physics-based gameplay is fun on its own, but in multiplayer it reaches another level. This game thrives on emergent gameplay and all the stuff that can happen thanks to how smartly items and enemies are designed. It’s peak “friendslop” for you and your buddies to try, so don’t miss out.

R.E.P.O is easily one of the better co-op games on Steam.

Far from “friend slop,” it’s got an addictive gameplay loop where every run feels different and never repetitive. The devs are extremely impressive with constant updates being released, frequent Q&As, and strong engagement with the community through suggestions and feedback.

The physics mixed with proximity chat and the unique abilities and characteristics of each monster make it extremely entertaining and fun with mates. We planned on playing the base game and then moving on to modded, but with the frequency of the updates and the content, we have not found a need to try modded yet.

If you want a game that delivers laughs, chaos, and chill sessions with friends, this is it. And for the price, you get an insane amount of value and playtime. Nominated 4 times for Steam Awards!

# R. E. P. O. - A liketype game done right - 8/10 (7)
Less than two years ago we got a little indie darling called Lethal company which blew up instantly, combining unique graphics from early gaming eras with horror and simple objectives and co-op at its core, its a great game but did falter in some places which I never felt really got addressed in its future updates. New games of this type would begin dropping shortly after, lethal company likes, murky divers, content warning and so on, while these put their new spin on the genre, I really wanted something similar to what lethal was but with a bit more nuance to it and I truly believe repo is showing that in already its early stages.

# GAMEPLAY
This loosely follows the same gameplay concept, you're collecting junk while avoiding monsters and if everyone dies, its game over. With each stage, the items needed go up and there's a vibrant ever changing shop to make runs more unique. 
Where repo is different is in one; its monster designs, they will always remain scary but after enough exposure, you can actually learn genuine tactics to survive them and even later on, find ways to kill them. 
All items are very fragile! you also get to use a cart, no more constantly running back and forth. And with everything being physics based, the possibilities of what you may pull off can be endless and I love games that can allow for that. 
While this is also a game that primarily works off using the proximity chat, the game does feature an inbuilt voice for those who wishes to only type, a good workaround for the ever annoying issue off squads who cant all talk into mics. 
Maps, monsters, items etc are always randomized making each attempt at reaching a new stage different and exciting, allowing you to try new ideas based on what you're given. There is also a revive mechanic, alongside a sharing health mechanic, this and the ability to hide from monsters to avoid death is what i think makes repo really interesting, setbacks don't feel as harsh and comebacks can be made with the right approached caution. Another massive plus is getting stat upgrades after levels, so alongside everything else, you can always get a new edge to go against the scaling difficulty. 

# DEV TEAM
Semiwork is the dev team behind this game and it is only their second game, originally starting out making skits on youtube, I grew up with these very skits and seeing those same people now make games I am growing to love is a really surreal and exciting experience as I am happy to see the same love and craft is still burning within them. They are also being incredibly open with the player base about the dev process, future updates and listening to feedback, as they aim to make this game for everyone, whether you're a seasoned pro or someone who would play occasionally. 

# Final thoughts
I will lobby two main negatives, one is a low amount of maps, even if they all have a lot of unique layouts, I think a game like this gets so much more value with good map variety and at launch, they only had 3, now there's 4 and I hope to see more added soon, luckily it has mod support. Because items can break, there is a risk of not enough loot existing in a level, ithink when it reaches this point, an alternative method should exist, soft locks are not fun. But neither of these are true gamebreakers, with how the game so far seems to wanna introduce innovation and not frustration, I'm very excited for its early access future which I wouldn't say about many games who chooses this path, an excellent game to play for choatic fun with friends.

R.E.P.O. is the kind of game that doesn’t take itself too seriously, and I love it for that. I jumped in with some friends expecting a solid extraction horror experience, and that’s exactly what we got—plus a lot of laughs.

The gameplay itself is intense, especially when things go south (which, let’s be real, they often do). You're tasked with navigating hostile environments, making crucial decisions under pressure, and managing resources—all while trying to avoid becoming the next target. The tension is real, but it’s the little moments of chaos that make it so much fun. Watching my friends run headfirst into danger, only to get swarmed by enemies or caught in traps, was hilarious (in a loving, “I told you so” kind of way).

What really stands out is how the game strikes a perfect balance between being scary and ridiculously fun. The mechanics are tight, and there’s enough strategy to keep things interesting, but it never takes itself too seriously. The absurdity of certain situations keeps the mood light, even when you're on the brink of failure.

All in all, R.E.P.O. is a great time if you're looking for a game that blends tension with plenty of humor. Grab a squad, dive in, and get ready for some chaotic fun!

After around [b]70 hours[/b], R.E.P.O. became one of my favorite co-op games.

The game really shines in later quotas, where tension, panic, and teamwork come together. Moments where half the team is down and you're desperately searching for the last items to finish the quota are where the game is at its best.

It can also be really funny with the right people, sometimes you're trying to take it seriously and actually survive, and other times everything just turns into complete chaos. Both ways are fun in their own way.

Even after taking breaks for months or even a year, this is the type of game that still pulls you back. It's perfect for relaxed evenings with friends instead of competitive games that can get frustrating.

The game is still in [b]early access[/b], but the developers are actively improving it and adding new content based on feedback, which is great to see.

If you have friends to play with, [b]I'd highly recommend it.[/b]
